stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
The content points to the ongoing community interest and adoption of Meta's Llama models.

stories.title: Here are the 30,000 songs Sony is suing Udio’s AI music generator over
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Sony Music is suing the AI music generator Udio over copyright infringement.
The lawsuit claims Udio infringed on over 30,000 songs, including major hits by Elvis Presley, Beyoncé, and Harry Styles.
This case highlights growing legal battles regarding AI training data and intellectual property rights in the music industry.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation and uses transformers and safetensors.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking of leading LLMs.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
Relevant tags confirm its use within the transformer architecture and its conversational capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 introduces significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in higher quality model outputs.
The updated engine also provides faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM integration.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, has integrated MLX for enhanced performance.
This update specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads for Apple hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview stage, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring that processing occurs entirely on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI capabilities for coding assistance.

stories.title: America needs to stop getting shocked by Chinese AI
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Chinese AI companies have released models claiming competitive parity with leading US systems (OpenAI, Anthropic).
The announcement triggered market volatility and significant commentary regarding the competitive landscape.
The event has reignited geopolitical discussions around AI development, framing it as a potential arms race.

stories.title: AliExpress hit with record $625M fine after failing to make EU-ordered fixes
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: AliExpress received a record $625M fine from EU regulators.
The fine stems from the platform's failure to implement required fixes under the Digital Services Act (DSA).
This highlights increasing regulatory scrutiny on major online retailers operating within the EU.

stories.title: Pay up or not? Ransomware surge has victims facing tough choices.
stories.author: Hannah Murphy, Financial Times
bullet_points: Ransomware attacks are increasing in sophistication, creating difficult choices for victims.
Governments are actively considering legislation to ban the practice of paying ransoms.
The trend signals a major shift in cybersecurity policy and threat response strategies.

stories.title: Differentiable Logic Gate Networks for Low-Latency EEG Classification on Edge Devices
stories.author: Camilo E. Valderrama
bullet_points: Introduces Differentiable Logic Gate Networks (Diff-Logic) as a hardware-native alternative to traditional floating-point neural networks for EEG classification.
Addresses the latency bottleneck of conventional models by compiling networks into pure Boolean circuits executable via bitwise CPU operations.
Demonstrates efficacy across multiple EEG datasets for tasks like dementia detection and emotion recognition on edge devices.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, complementing the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: Who’s afraid of the big, bad GPU?
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The article questions the perceived value of GPUs driving AI advancements.
It raises environmental concerns regarding the energy and water consumption of data centers.
The piece prompts readers to consider the societal impact (excitement vs. anxiety) of generative AI.

stories.title: The FCC is planning to retroactively ban disguised DJI gadgets
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The FCC is preparing to use its authority to retroactively ban certain gadgets.
The crackdown specifically targets devices from 'DJI front companies' suspected of non-compliance.
This action represents the first application of the FCC's newly acquired retroactive banning power.

stories.title: SpaceX in your index fund, explained
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: The article discusses the implications of high-risk, high-reward companies like SpaceX being included in traditionally 'safe' investment vehicles like index funds.
It raises a critical question about the risk profile when speculative giants are integrated into broad market indices (e.g., Nasdaq-100).
The piece serves as a cautionary discussion on the valuation and risk inherent in modern tech investing, using SpaceX as a case study.

stories.title: Firefighting drones in the works as wildfires plague US nearly year-round
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Development of firefighting drones is underway to combat persistent wildfires in the US.
The XPRIZE competition is being used to test the efficacy of these drones in early wildfire intervention.
The initiative highlights the application of advanced robotics and technology to critical environmental challenges.

stories.title: Judge halts Paramount's $111B purchase of Warner Bros. in win for US states
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A judge has issued a restraining order against Paramount's proposed $111B acquisition of Warner Bros.
The legal action is based on the finding that the merger is 'likely to violate antitrust laws.'
The ruling represents a significant win for US states challenging the large media consolidation.

stories.title: The Space Force is now seeking to buy up to $30 billion in rocket launches
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The Space Force is tasked with a significant procurement effort.
The scope of the procurement involves up to $30 billion in rocket launches.
The increased demand is linked to directives from the Trump administration.

stories.title: Simple Domain Generalization for Strong Pixel-Level Image Tampering Detection in Modern VLMs
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses the growing challenge of detecting pixel-level image tampering in modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) like Gemini and ChatGPT.
Focuses on Domain Generalization to ensure tampering detection models remain robust across different VLM-generated manipulation styles (out-of-distribution shifts).
Aims to develop localization models capable of reliably identifying tampering regardless of the specific VLM used for image generation/editing.

stories.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Efficient Pathology Foundation Models for Whole-Slide and Tumor Microenvironment Analysis
stories.author: Hoifung Poon
bullet_points: Introduces GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, new efficient foundation models for computational pathology.
Addresses limitations of existing models, such as tile-level operation, restrictive licensing, and high computational cost.
Focuses on applying foundation models to analyze whole-slide images and the tumor microenvironment for cancer diagnosis and prognosis.

stories.title: Learning Adaptive Safety Margins for Visual Navigation
stories.author: Yi Fang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical issue in robotic navigation: the failure of fixed safety margins in cluttered environments.
Proposes a novel 'context-conditioned safety critic' to learn adaptive clearance preferences for planners.
Focuses on improving trajectory selection from diverse candidates generated by diffusion-based planners using RGB-D data.

stories.title: TRIM: Reducing AI-Generated CodeSlop via Agent Trajectory Minimization
stories.author: Baishakhi Ray
bullet_points: The paper addresses the issue of 'codeSlop'—AI-generated code being unnecessarily verbose compared to human code.
The root cause is identified as the agent's internal search process, where speculative and abandoned edits accumulate.
The proposed method, TRIM, aims to reduce this code bloat by minimizing the agent's trajectory during code generation.

stories.title: LLMs and Agentic AI Systems for Smart Grids: A Tutorial on Architectures and Applications
stories.author: Yuanyuan Shi
bullet_points: The paper discusses the application of LLMs and agentic AI systems to complex technical domains like smart grids.
These systems are being used for grid functions such as forecasting, optimization, and control by interfacing with traditional solvers.
A key gap identified is the lack of a unified methodology for designing and evaluating these LLM-based agentic systems.

stories.title: The Many Senses of Visual Similarity: A Text-Prompted Image Perceptual Metric
stories.author: Richard Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in current perceptual similarity metrics by acknowledging context-dependent human visual judgments.
Introduces a large-scale dataset of human similarity judgments annotated across multiple, free-form semantic aspects.
Aims to allow similarity metrics to be conditioned on specific visual aspects (e.g., shape vs. color).

stories.title: Patch Policy: Efficient Embodied Control via Dense Visual Representations
stories.author: Lerrel Pinto
bullet_points: The paper addresses the underutilization of dense visual features from Vision Transformers (ViTs) in robot learning.
Current robot policies often either use single global tokens or train visual backbones from scratch, losing spatial detail and pre-training benefits.
The proposed 'Patch Policy' aims to create efficient embodied control by leveraging dense patch features without incurring the heavy computational cost of existing VLA models.

stories.title: Causal Discovery on Irregular Time Series
stories.author: Pedro Bizarro
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in causal discovery methods: their reliance on regular time series data.
The paper proposes an extension of the PCMCI+ method to handle irregularly sampled streams of events.
This work is highly relevant to real-world applications like sensor data, healthcare monitoring, and financial transaction analysis.

stories.title: Vector Search As Nearest Neighbor Matching: RAG-based Policy Learning in Causal Inference
stories.author: Taka Kato
bullet_points: Proposes novel one-step and two-step methods for policy learning utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Formulates RAG-based action selection within the established potential outcome framework for causal inference.
The two-step method integrates vector search to retrieve neighboring evidence, followed by a generator estimating outcomes and a rule selecting the final action.

stories.title: PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning
stories.author: Warren J. Gross
bullet_points: Introduces PPL-Factory, a new method for task-aware and budget-aware data selection during LLM fine-tuning.
Addresses the inefficiency of current data selection methods, which rely on fixed, non-generalizable heuristics (e.g., data quality, diversity).
Aims to reduce computational costs in LLM training while maintaining or improving downstream task performance.

stories.title: Three-Body Scattering for Generative Modeling
stories.author: Tao Lin
bullet_points: Introduces Three-Body Scattering Modeling (TBSM) as an alternative to standard generative model architectures (e.g., adversarial, autoregressive).
Proposes using a distributional energy to induce sample-level motion and provide direct, one-step regression supervision.
The core mechanism models interactions as constant-size per-projectile attractions and repulsions toward/from real sources.

stories.title: Certified Training for Convolutional Perturbations
stories.author: Alessio Lomuscio
bullet_points: Vision models are vulnerable to real-world perturbations, such as motion blur from camera shake.
Current robustness methods (e.g., data augmentation, Adversarial Training) lack formal safety guarantees.
The research proposes 'Certified Training' to provide formal guarantees against these perturbations for critical applications.

stories.title: EVOLVE: Efficient Learned Volume Compression with Variable-Rate Encoding on a Cross-Domain Database
stories.author: Chaoli Wang
bullet_points: EVOLVE is a new autoencoder-based method designed for efficient, lossy compression of large-scale volumetric data from scientific simulations.
It addresses limitations in existing compressors, specifically the difficulty in preserving fine structural details at high compression ratios (CRs).
The method incorporates variable-rate encoding, offering an improvement over Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) which typically have fixed CRs.

stories.title: FlashRT: Agent Harness for Guiding Agents to Deploy Real-Time Multimodal Applications
stories.author: Beidi Chen
bullet_points: Introduces FlashRT, an agent harness designed to guide the deployment of real-time multimodal applications.
Addresses the complexity of deploying heterogeneous models (like voice agents and video generation) which require application-specific decisions on parallelism and streaming.
Overcomes limitations of existing serving systems that rely on fixed workload assumptions, reducing the need for manual, hand-crafted optimizations.

stories.title: It's Not What You Say, It's How You Say It: Evaluating LLM Responses to Expressions of Belief
stories.author: Alex Warstadt
bullet_points: The research addresses how Large Language Models (LLMs) should handle user-expressed beliefs (EoBs).
It investigates that the linguistic form of belief expression (e.g., presuppositions, certainty markers) affects how the LLM processes it.
The study proposes a typology to systematically evaluate the persuasiveness and impact of different EoB styles on LLM behavior.

stories.title: SWE-Pruner Pro: The Coder LLM Already Knows What to Prune
stories.author: Xiaodong Gu
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Pruner Pro, a new method for context pruning in coding LLMs.
The core innovation is leveraging the LLM's internal representations to determine code context relevance, rather than relying on external classifiers.
This allows for direct pruning of tool outputs within the agent itself, improving context management efficiency.

stories.title: PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning
stories.author: Warren J. Gross
bullet_points: The research introduces 'PPL-Factory,' a method for task-aware and budget-aware data selection during LLM fine-tuning.
It addresses the inefficiency of using all training samples by selecting only the most informative ones to reduce computational cost.
The method aims to overcome the limitations of existing, fixed heuristics (like data quality or diversity) by using perplexity-based selection.

stories.title: Do Language Models Dream of Binding Molecules? Benchmarking LLMs under Spatial Constraints
stories.author: Alex Zhavoronkov
bullet_points: The research investigates the capability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to handle 3D spatial constraints in molecular design.
It addresses the gap in LLMs' ability to reason about physics and 3D environments, a critical aspect of Structure-based Drug Design (SBDD).
The work benchmarks LLMs against established diffusion models in the context of generating binding molecules for protein targets.

stories.title: O-VAD: Industrial Video Anomaly Detection through Object-Centric Tracking and Reasoning
stories.author: Min Xu
bullet_points: The paper addresses Industrial Video Anomaly Detection (IVAD), a critical area for modern manufacturing and quality control.
It identifies a limitation in current Vision-Language Model (VLM) methods, noting their performance drop in complex industrial settings.
The proposed O-VAD method focuses on object-centric tracking and reasoning to handle intricate object transformations and procedural constraints.

stories.title: How Does Alignment Tuning Shape Representations of Sycophancy and Related Cue-Induced Biases in LLMs?
stories.author: Zhijing Jin
bullet_points: The research investigates how alignment tuning influences LLM representations of biases like sycophancy.
It addresses the vulnerability of LLMs to subtle prompt changes (e.g., hints, fake examples) that can flip correct answers.
The study extracts per-bias directions from hidden states across multiple model families to pinpoint where these biases reside.

stories.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
stories.author: Furu Wei
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in RL fine-tuning where LLM-as-a-Judge discards rich textual feedback by converting evaluations into scalar rewards.
Introduces 'Experiential Learning' (EL) to repurpose the LLM's assessment from a judge to a 'coach'.
The coach distills assessment into transferable knowledge to condition a teacher model and improve the policy.

stories.title: Python 3.15's Ultra-Low Overhead Interpreter Profiling Mode – Ken Jin's Blog
stories.author: rbanffy
bullet_points: Python 3.15 introduces an ultra-low overhead interpreter profiling mode.
The feature is detailed in a blog post by Ken Jin.
This suggests improvements in performance analysis for Python development.

stories.title: 432 Linux kernel CVEs published in the last 24 hours
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via Helithumper
bullet_points: A large volume of 432 new CVEs (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) related to the Linux kernel were published recently.
This indicates a high rate of vulnerability discovery and disclosure within the Linux kernel ecosystem.
The news is highly relevant to system administrators, security professionals, and developers relying on Linux infrastructure.

stories.title: AI And Code Ownership: Who Is Responsible For Generated Code?
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: The article addresses the complex legal question of code ownership when AI generates software.
It highlights the ambiguity surrounding intellectual property rights for AI-assisted code.
This topic represents a growing, moderate industry discussion point in software development.

stories.title: Stop Letting AI Write Security Bugs: Introducing "hallint"
stories.author: asyncinnovator
bullet_points: Addresses the growing reliance on AI coding assistants (Copilot, ChatGPT) for development.
Introduces 'hallint,' a tool designed to prevent AI-generated code from containing security vulnerabilities.
Highlights the industry challenge of balancing coding speed with code security in the age of generative AI.
